title: A note on the monotonicity of observational ergotropic advantage
authors: Debanjan Dey Sarkar, Mallika Mondal, Preeti Parashar
abstract: Very recently, Mahanti et al. (arXiv:2609.18735) introduced the observational ergotropic advantage, which gives the maximum value of extra work that a measurement can obtain with respect to all incoherent measurements. However, the above quantity does not show monotonic behaviour under the resource theory of measurement coherence. So, the search for a resource theory in which it is a monotone was open. We derive the monotonicity of this quantity using energy-preserving channels and passive resets as free operations and energy-incoherent measurements as free objects. We show the monotonicity property of the measure as a necessary criterion of measurement transformation, but it turns out not to be a sufficient condition. It is further established that the measure is not convex. A short analysis of bounds and tightness of the measure using a degenerate Hamiltonian is also given.
summary: This paper develops a resource theory framework to analyze the monotonicity of the observational ergotropic advantage ($	ext{WH}_{	ext{adv}}(M)$) in quantum systems. By defining specific free operations, the authors prove that $	ext{WH}_{	ext{adv}}(M)$ is monotonic under these rules. Crucially, they establish that this monotonicity is only a necessary, but not sufficient, condition for measurement transformations.
main_problem: The paper investigates establishing a resource theory framework where the observational ergotropic advantage ($	ext{WH}_{	ext{adv}}(M)$) exhibits monotonicity.
main_result: The authors successfully derive the monotonicity of $	ext{WH}_{	ext{adv}}(M)$ using energy-preserving channels and passive resets as free operations. However, they prove this monotonicity is a necessary but not sufficient condition for measurement transformation, and the measure is not convex.
method: The analysis relies on constructing a resource theory by defining free operations (Energy-Preserving Channels and Passive Resets) and free objects (energy-incoherent measurements) to prove the monotonicity property.
model_or_system: The study concerns quantum systems governed by a Hamiltonian $H = \sum_l E_l |E_langle\langle E_l|$, focusing on the work extractable via measurements and operations.
key_observables: Observational Ergotropic Advantage ($	ext{WH}_{	ext{adv}}(M)$), Ergotropy ($	ext{W}_{	ext{erg}}(ho)$), and work extractable using measurements ($	ext{W}_{	ext{obs}}(ho, M)$).
important_parameters: Energy-preserving channels (EPCPR) and passive resets are key operations defining the resource theory.
main_assumptions: The primary assumptions involve defining the free operations and free objects to impose the necessary monotonicity condition on the measure.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the observational ergotropic advantage and notes its lack of monotonicity under standard theories. It then proposes a resource theory using EPCPR and energy-incoherent measurements to derive the monotonicity (Theorem 2). Finally, it establishes that this necessary condition is not sufficient and that the measure lacks convexity (Theorem 3).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses resource theories in quantum thermodynamics, which is crucial for understanding the fundamental limits of work extraction and information processing in open quantum systems.
